scope: Theorem 7.1 (Geometric conclusion) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-the-Kadison-Kaplansky-Projection-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df6227b615985805), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C∗, C• such that, for suffi- ciently large ℓ, the preceding hypotheses have the following consequences. Every component map ϕ : C → X is an embedding. Index copies by pairs (C, ϕ) modulo the equivalence (C, ϕ) ∼ (δaC, ϕδ−1 a ), a ∈ F. Thus an indexed copy Q remembers its source component and source vertices up to this deck align- ment, in addition to its embedded image. There is a well-order of these copies and an induced intrinsic ball B(Q) in each Q such that 1. every vertex of Q shared with an earlier copy belongs to B(Q); 2. the subgraph of Q consisting of all edges with at least one endpoint in B(Q) is a forest; 3. for every vertex of B(Q) lying over layer i, |V (B(Q))| ≤ wi, wi = 2C•Hi ; (7.4) 4. if DQ is V (Q) minus its vertices shared with earlier copies, the domains DQ are pairwise disjoint, and deleting every edge of Q whose two endpoints lie in DQ, for all Q, leaves a forest in X. Furthermore Γproj is torsion-free. None of the constants depends on F, the voltage values, the number of components of P, or |S|.
